This model in my 2020 RAV4 handled strong winds gusting at 40+ MPH while I was driving over 80 MPH on the freeway, no wind related interventions and never once left the lane or even touched a lane line in 600 miles, while I'm watching nearly everyone else on the road getting pushed around. So I'll give it credit for being the best wind resistant model I've ever used, noticably better than GWM9.

However, lead following is a bit weird and the steering is all over the place at low speeds (seems much better above 60 MPH). So it has long and lat issues.

Even aggressive stays way too far away from the lead when going above 65 MPH or so, like an entire football field, it's so far it's almost funny.

But the strangest part is the way it locks in the following distance based on speed. Like it's a spacecraft stationkeeping another spacecraft, it will accelerate or brake swiftly to stay a precise distance away from the lead car based on speed. If the lead speeds up or slows down, it has this almost magical ability to instantly speed up to maintain the same following distance. It's especially noticeable at high speeds.

But there is one major issue that is going to make me switch to a different model, the ping ponging at low speeds. Below 50 MPH or so, it will move around like "this is my lane and I'm gonna use all of it". Firehose hugs the left but CGWM hugs the whole road 😂. It gets way too close to the line in city driving, so for that reason, I can't use it since I do a lot of city driving delivering for Amazon.

Overall, it's a very good model on the highway if you like a lot of following distance, but at low speeds it's unreliable and any sort of low speed curves are about as much of a gamble as a slot machine.
